candidates.explanation: Board clearly owns orchestration and policy; board-owned ports and adapters target narrow public capability APIs; dependencies remain acyclic; the route uses the board RSC surface; authorization and single-boundary unexpected-failure reporting are explicit.

The board slice coherently owns policy and orchestration, uses board-local ports with outbound adapters to public server APIs, preserves capability isolation, exposes one RSC-facing DAL entrypoint, and specifies fail-closed authorization plus report-once failure handling.

Board ownership, acyclic capability isolation, the RSC-facing board entrypoint, authorization, and report-once behavior are clear. Dependency seams are only partially aligned with the rubric because board directly consumes capability operations and explicitly omits board-owned ports/adapters.

Board owns the cross-capability policy, capability internals remain isolated, and the route calls a board query. However, board directly consumes capability DTO APIs without board-owned ports/adapters, and unexpected-failure logging is described without a clear single reporting owner or explicit report-once guarantee.
